Phuket101 Patong (4 Oct 2026), Kalim (12 Mar 2026) and Illuzion (29 Aug 2026: 20+, passport, no flip-flops). Lion hours from Google, Value Plus Sansabai 09:00-04:00 from the Value Plus branch API. Pin: Google 'Patong Beach' 13 m, Wikidata 50 m, on the OSM beach. Old gmapsQuery opened the Pa Tong subdistrict, not the beach.

items.name: Kamala
items.tagline: Calm family beach with Café del Mar at the north end
items.description: A long, wide beach by a Muslim fishing village, calmer and more Thai than Patong. Families, couples and repeat visitors like it. Café del Mar at the quiet north end books big house and techno DJs in season. Apart from Café del Mar, nights are quiet; Phuket FantaSea and Carnival Magic are the big evening shows.
items.beach: About 2 km of soft sand with tree shade. In January the sea is usually calm and clear, one of the easiest swims on the island.
highlights: Argy on the Café del Mar Pyramid Stage, Fri 8 Jan from 14:00 (presale sign-up opens 20 Oct, 18:00)
Marco Carola, with Nicolas Masseyeff, at Café del Mar, Wed 13 Jan from 14:00
Café del Mar Club Room DJ nights, Wed-Sat from 22:00
Sunset drinks at Pine Beach Bar (InterContinental) at the north end
Phuket FantaSea show: Tue, Fri and Sun, show at 21:00
items.coordSource: osm-beach(relation 6892478)+google(Kamala Beach, 70 m)+wikidata(Q10542974, 65 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Kamala Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a calm beach, Café del Mar on foot, and Shelter, Niky's and Enthusiast Place within about 20 minutes by car.
tips: Sign up or buy tickets early on phuket.cafedelmar.com. Loungers and beds work on a minimum spend.
Carnival Magic, next to FantaSea, runs on Mon, Wed and Sat evenings.
Kamala and Patong are linked by one hill road; after a party use Grab or Bolt.
items.verification: Café del Mar events page (15 Oct 2026): the 8 Jan Pyramid Stage night is now Argy (presale 20 Oct 18:00), so it is no longer secret; Marco Carola 13 Jan 14:00 on the venue site and RA (with Nicolas Masseyeff); Club Room 'Wed-Sat 10pm-late'. Phuket101 Café del Mar (29 Aug 2026): north end, minimum spend for beds. FantaSea days from its official site and Google (Tue/Fri/Sun); Carnival Magic Mon/Wed/Sat from Google and Phuket101 Kamala (5 Oct 2026). Pine Beach Bar on Google at the north end. Pin: OSM beach mid-section; Google 70 m, Wikidata 65 m.

items.name: Surin & Pansea
items.tagline: One of Phuket's best beaches, now with nothing on the sand
items.description: An 800 m bay of soft pale sand between Kamala and Bang Tao, with casuarina trees behind it. All food stalls, sunbeds and massages were removed in May 2025, so it looks natural again. Tukta, on the rocks at the south end, is one of only two places still serving food. Twinpalms, The Surin and Amanpuri are close.
items.beach: In January the water is clear and calm, some of the best swimming in Phuket. There are no sunbeds or umbrellas, so bring water and sit in the tree shade.
highlights: Morning swim in clear, calm water
Lunch with a view at Tukta, on the rocks at the south end
Laem Singh Beach: a 15-20 minute walk over the rocks, or a 100 THB boat
Sunset under the casuarina trees
items.coordSource: osm-beach(relation 14010442)+google(Surin Beach, 37 m)+wikidata(Q14925036, 15 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Surin Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a quiet luxury hotel on a beautiful beach and will take taxis for food and parties.
tips: Come in the morning and bring water; there are no sunbeds or shops on the sand.
Laem Singh has had no road access since April 2017. Walk over the boulders from the south end of Surin (not at high tide) or take a boat, about 100 THB one way.
Pansea Beach, just north, is only for guests of The Surin and Amanpuri.
items.verification: Phuket101 Surin (16 Sep 2026): vendors removed since May 2025, Tukta is 'one of the two restaurants still operating', Pansea is guests-only. Phuket101 Laem Singh (4 Aug 2026): road cut April 2017, 15-20 min walk, boat 100 THB. Tukta Food & Drink, The Surin, Twinpalms and Amanpuri all active on Google. Catch Beach Club is on Bang Tao, so it was dropped from Surin highlights. Pin: Google 37 m, Wikidata 15 m, OSM beach midpoint. Note: the only photo is from 2008, before the clear-outs.

items.name: Bang Tao, Laguna & Cherngtalay
items.tagline: Long beach, top restaurants, beach clubs and Niky's
items.description: A 6 km beach with the Laguna resort complex in the middle and Cherngtalay town behind it. The upmarket side of Phuket: villas, Michelin-listed restaurants and Boat Avenue's shops and bars. Catch and Xana beach clubs have DJs, and Niky's Speakeasy & Nightclub plays house and techno until 02:00. Traffic is often bad.
items.beach: In January the sea is mostly calm, but the water gets deep faster than at many beaches. The beach is never crowded. In mid-2026 the authorities shut the beach bars on the south stretch, between SAii Laguna and Arinara.
highlights: Catch Beach Club: DJ daybeds, Friday BBQ (19:00-22:00) and Sunday brunch (12:00-15:00)
Niky's Speakeasy & Nightclub: house and techno, Tue-Sun 20:00-02:00
Fun Friday Avenue night market at Boat Avenue (Fri 16:00-21:00)
Enthusiast Place: free Open Doors music session every Tuesday from 19:00, about 15 minutes inland
items.coordSource: osm-beach(way 150298518) midpoint+wikidata(Q16306319, 47 m); Google pin 660 m south on the same beach
items.gmapsQuery: Bang Tao Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want great food and beach clubs, Niky's nearby and a 30-minute ride to the airport, and do not need a party street.
tips: Niky's website was offline in Oct 2026; check its Google Maps listing for the night's programme.
Value Plus has an exchange booth on Lagoon Road near Boat Avenue (09:00-20:00).
Leave extra time for traffic around Cherngtalay, especially in the evening.
items.verification: Phuket101 Bang Tao (5 Oct 2026): 6 km, calm in high season, 'not as shallow', never crowded, bars between SAii Laguna and Arinara shut in 2026 (16 venues named in a June 2026 investigation; a Thairath report of 26 June 2026 says 16 shops were ordered shut). Catch site: DJ daybeds, Fri BBQ 19-22, Sun brunch 12-15, on Bang Tao. Niky's: Google listing active, Tue-Sun 20:00-02:00, owner text says techno and house; one Tripadvisor review (May 2025) says 'house & techno'; nikys-speakeasy.com did not connect (15 Oct 2026). Enthusiast Place site: Open Doors every Tuesday 19:00, free. Boat Avenue market Fri 16-21 (Phuket101 + Google). Value Plus Laguna 09:00-20:00 from its API; its Phuket rates are not published, so the rate comment was removed. Pin: OSM midpoint, Wikidata 47 m.

items.name: Layan
items.tagline: Quiet north end of Bang Tao with an island and a river
items.description: The quiet north end of Bang Tao Bay, inside Sirinat National Park. The beach ends at a river mouth with a big wooded island in front. The small restaurants under the trees were removed; only Tan Restaurant & Massage is left. Anantara Layan and other luxury villas sit just north of the river. Very quiet at night.
items.beach: In January the sea is usually calm and good for a swim. Massages are still offered, but there is almost no food or drink on the sand, so bring water.
highlights: The wooded island and river mouth at the north end of the beach
Sunset drinks at Beach House Layan (Anantara), which has a rooftop bar
Walk south along the sand onto Bang Tao Beach
Daft Funk Live (Daft Punk tribute band) at Banana Beach Club, Thu 14 Jan from 17:00, 10 minutes north by car (fun, not underground)
items.coordSource: google(Layan Beach, 171 m)+osm(Layan beach Restaurant node, 78 m)+google(Sirinat NP unit Hat Layan, 67 m)+commons photo GPS (121 m)+esri imagery
items.gmapsQuery: Layan Beach, Thalang, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a peaceful villa or resort near the airport and Bang Tao, and will take taxis for nights out.
tips: For the public beach, follow the signs to Banyan Tree from Bang Tao and drive to the very end of the road; it is narrow in places.
Anantara Layan and Beach House face a small cove north of the river mouth; the long public beach is south of it.
Bang Tao's restaurants and Niky's are 10-15 minutes away by car.
items.verification: Re-pinned 849 m. The old pin was the OSM 'Layan Beach' way, which is the small Anantara cove north of the river mouth. Google's 'Layan Beach', the Sirinat park unit 'Hat Layan', Tan Restaurant & Massage (Phuket101, 26 Aug 2026: the last restaurant on Layan Beach), the OSM 'Layan beach Restaurant' and the GPS of the Commons 'Layan beach' photo all sit on the public beach south of the river; imagery confirms sand at the new point. So the old tip that Google's pin was wrong was itself wrong. Inside Sirinat NP per the OSM park boundary. Daft Funk on Megatix: Thu 14 Jan 17:00, Banana Beach Club by Sollis 2.0 (OSRM 6 min from the beach). Beach House Layan (Rooftop, Dee Plee, Breeze) on its site, open 12-22 on Google.

items.name: Nai Thon
items.tagline: Quiet bay under green hills, 15 minutes from the airport
items.description: A small curved bay below steep hills, inside Sirinat National Park. There is no real town, just a few hotels, guesthouses and simple Thai restaurants along the beach. Quiet day and night. Banana Beach, 2 km south, changed in late 2025: the old jungle path closed, and a car park (100 THB) and a big beach club opened.
items.beach: In January the sea is calm and the bay is good for swimming, with fine sand and few people.
highlights: Swim in a calm, uncrowded bay
Banana Beach and Banana Beach Club, 2 km south (parking 100 THB)
Simple Thai meals at the small restaurants by the beach
Short ride to Nai Yang and the plane-spotting beach
items.coordSource: osm-beach(way 53166566) midpoint+photon(12 m); Google pin and a Commons photo GPS 300 m north on the same beach
items.gmapsQuery: Nai Thon Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a quiet beach close to the airport for your first or last nights.

links.label: Wikivoyage: Nai Thon and Nai Yang

items.verification: Phuket101 Banana Beach (13 Aug 2026): old hilltop path closed late 2025, new car park 100 THB, new beach club; Google and Megatix name it Banana Beach Club by Sollis 2.0 (4.7, 863 reviews, 1.7 km from this pin). Phuket101 Sirinat page and the OSM park boundary put Nai Thon inside the park. Sources disagree on whether the restaurants are on the sand (Wikivoyage) or across the road (Lonely Planet, checked), so the text now says 'along the beach'. Patong time kept at 40 min (OSRM 34 min without traffic). Pin: OSM beach midpoint; Google 300 m north on the same beach.

items.name: Nai Yang
items.tagline: Beach restaurants and planes, 10 minutes from the airport
items.description: A relaxed beach village next to the airport, inside Sirinat National Park. Casuarina trees give shade, and simple restaurants put tables on the sand. It has an old-Phuket feel. There is a coral reef off the beach, and the plane-spotting spot at the end of the runway is close. Nightlife is a few small bars.
items.beach: In January the sea is calm, but the water is very shallow and less blue than further south; it is nicer at the north end of the bay.
highlights: Dinner at a restaurant on the sand
Planes landing low over the south end of Mai Khao Beach
Snorkel off the beach near the park lifeguard post (dry season)
Shade and picnics in Sirinat National Park
items.coordSource: osm-beach(way 1020477061)+google(Naiyang Beach, 45 m)+commons photo GPS (14 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Naiyang Beach, Thalang, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you have an early flight or want simple beach food and a local feel near the airport.
tips: Money Shop Exchange has an office in Nai Yang, open about 10:00-19:00 (OK rates, lower than the best changers).
items.verification: Phuket101 Nai Yang (30 Sep 2026): casuarina shade, beach restaurants (The Good View, Sea Almond), very shallow water, nicer in the north, minimal nightlife, standing in the landing path is forbidden. Reef and snorkelling from the lifeguard post from Wikivoyage; other guides also describe a reef close to shore, partly bleached. Money Shop Nai Yang active on Google (4.8), 10:00-19:00. Pin: OSM beach, Google 'Naiyang Beach' 45 m. The old gmapsQuery returned two pins, one of them 2.3 km north by the runway; 'Naiyang Beach, Thalang, Phuket' returns only the right one.

items.name: Mai Khao
items.tagline: 11 km of empty sand, big resorts and landing planes
items.description: Phuket's longest beach, 11 km, inside Sirinat National Park. No chairs, vendors or jet skis, just a few big resorts set back from the sand, such as Sala, Renaissance, JW Marriott and Anantara. Sea turtles sometimes nest here from November to February. Patong is an hour away, and there is nothing to walk to at night.
items.beach: January is the calmest month here, but there are no shops or chairs on the sand, so bring water and sun cream for long walks.
highlights: Plane spotting at the south end of the beach
Long, empty beach walks at sunset
Turtle nesting season, November to February (nests are rare)
Splash Jungle Waterpark (daily 10:00-18:30)
items.coordSource: osm-beach(relation 16031134) midpoint+wikidata(Q14223640, 108 m); Google pin 1.3 km south on the same beach
items.gmapsQuery: Mai Khao Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a big resort on an empty beach close to the airport and do not plan many nights out.
tips: Standing in the planes' landing path is officially forbidden; watch from the side, not on the runway line.

imageCandidates.source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:หาดทรายขาว_น้ำใส_คลื่นสวย.jpg

items.verification: Phuket101 Mai Khao (26 Sep 2026): 11 km, no chairs/vendors except near the runway, no jet skis, Sala/Renaissance/JW Marriott, nesting Nov-Feb; Wikivoyage: calmest sea around January. All four resorts active on Google. Splash Jungle site: 'open daily (until further notice) 10:00-18:30'. Landing-path rule from Phuket101 (signs in the park). Pin: OSM midpoint, Wikidata 108 m, so confidence raised to high.

items.name: Karon
items.tagline: Big, open beach with a relaxed small town
items.description: A wide 3 km beach with a road and promenade behind it, so it never feels crowded. Most hotels are across the road, and the small town has beer bars, live music and good-value restaurants. Families and repeat visitors like it. The dry sand squeaks under your feet. Patong is about 15 minutes north and Kata is next door.
items.beach: In January the sea is usually calm and good for swimming; the strong rip currents here are a May-October problem, but still check the flags.
highlights: Karon Temple Market (Tue and Fri, 16:00-22:00)
Sunset fire show at Tann Beach Club (19:00)
Sunset drinks at COAST Beach Club, Centara Grand
Dinner along the beachfront promenade
items.coordSource: osm-beach(way 134394729)+google(Karon Beach, 26 m)+wikidata(Q13424404, 170 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Karon Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a big, calm beach and good value, with Patong's clubs about 15 minutes away.
tips: The quietest sand is at the north end, near the lake.
Money Shop Exchange has offices in Karon and Kata (OK rates).

imageCandidates.credit: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

items.verification: Phuket101 Karon (5 Oct 2026): 3.3 km, promenade, squeaky sand, quieter north end by the lake, swim Dec-May and serious rips May-Oct, Tann fire show 19:00 nightly, COAST at Centara Grand. Temple Market Tue and Fri 16:00-22:00 (Phuket101, 14 Mar 2026). Tann Beach Club (4.5) and Coast Beach Club & Bistro (4.4) active on Google; Money Shop Karon and Kata on Google. Pin: Google 26 m, Wikidata 170 m, OSM beach midpoint.

items.name: Kata (Kata Yai)
items.tagline: Beautiful bay with an island; busy, easy and walkable
items.description: One of Phuket's most beautiful beaches, with soft sand, blue water and Koh Pu, a small island in the bay. It is busy, but nightlife is calm: beer bars, a night market and sunset bars. Club Med fills about 90% of the beachfront, so you reach the sand from the two ends. Many restaurants and hotels, from budget to luxury.
items.beach: In January the sea is calm, clear and good for swimming (the surf and red-flag season is about June to November); the north end is the quietest part.
highlights: Sunset with Koh Pu island in front of the beach
Ska Bar under its big tree at the south end
Kata Night Market (daily, 14:00-23:00)
Karon Viewpoint over three bays, about 3 km south
items.coordSource: osm-beach(relation 4235947)+wikidata(Q14220372, 97 m)+google(Kata Beach, 136 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Kata Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if the beach matters most and you want an easy, walkable area with many restaurants.
tips: Shops and restaurants are on the second road; the beach road is quiet because Club Med fills the beachfront.
items.verification: Phuket101 Kata (5 Oct 2026): Koh Pu, Club Med on 90% of the beachfront with access from the two ends, surf and unsafe swimming June-November, quieter north end, beer bars, Kata Night Market 14:00-23:00 daily, Ska Bar, Karon Viewpoint about 3 km. Ska Bar (10:00-01:00), the night market, Club Med and Karon Viewpoint active on Google. The 'busiest after Patong' claim had no source and was removed. Pin: OSM midpoint, Wikidata 97 m, Google 136 m.

items.name: Kata Noi
items.tagline: Small, clear bay shared by only three resorts
items.description: An 850 m bay just south of Kata, behind a rocky headland. Only three resorts share it (Katathani, The Shore and Mom Tri's Villa Royale), so it stays calm. There is no town; Kata's restaurants are a short ride away. The hill road above has sunset bars with a view of the bay: After Beach Bar, The Sundeck and Fira.
items.beach: From November to April the sea is flat and very clear, one of the best swims in Phuket. Lifeguards watch the beach in the day. Sunbeds are only for resort guests, so bring a towel and use the shade at either end.
highlights: Swim in flat, clear water
Sunset at After Beach Bar or The Sundeck
Fira Beach Club on the hill
Short ride to Kata for dinner
items.coordSource: osm-beach(relation 4235946, 17 m)+wikidata(Q13424403, 23 m)+google(Kata Noi Beach, 26 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Kata Noi Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a calm, beautiful swimming beach and sunset bars, and do not need nightlife.
tips: Parking is small; in high season arrive before 10:00 or come by Bolt or Grab.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket101 Kata Noi page (updated 16 Sep 2026) confirms the 850 m beach, three resorts, the sunset bars, daytime lifeguards, no public sunbeds and small parking. Google Maps: beach 4.6 (3,017 reviews); Fira Beach Club, After Beach Bar and The Sundeck listed with current hours. Pin = OSM beach midpoint; Wikidata 23 m and Google 26 m away. OSRM free-flow: airport 53 min, Patong 15 min.

items.name: Nai Harn
items.tagline: Green hills, a lake and a protected beach in the south
items.description: A wide, soft beach between green hills, with a lake and a temple behind it and yachts in the bay. By law nothing can be built on the land behind the sand, so there are only tall casuarina trees. No town, just scattered restaurants, cafes and villas, with many long-stay expats. Busy in Dec-Jan, but relaxed.
items.beach: In January the water is clear blue and calm, one of the best swimming beaches in the south, but this is its busiest time of year.
highlights: Windmill Viewpoint over Ya Nui and Promthep
Black Rock Viewpoint (steep climb)
Ao Sane, a small snorkelling cove (one 2026 guide said it was closed for building work; check first)
Wat Nai Harn and the lake (paddle boats)
Reflections rooftop bar at The Nai Harn (17:00-22:00)
items.coordSource: osm-beach(relation 6162518, 31 m)+google(Nai Han Beach, 78 m)+wikidata(Q14226240, 100 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Nai Han Beach (หาดในหาน), Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want nature, a great beach and a calm long-stay feel, and do not mind 30 minutes to Patong.
tips: Google's English 'Nai Harn Beach' result is a locality pin almost 1 km north-east of the sand. The Thai name หาดในหาน (Google: 'Nai Han Beach') lands on the beach.
Money Shop Exchange has an office in Nai Harn (daily 10:00-19:00 on Google; OK rates, a little below Mamy Exchange).
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket101 Nai Harn page (updated 15 Sep 2026): protected land behind the sand, paddle boats on the lake, viewpoints, Reflections rooftop, busy in Dec-Jan. Google test: 'Nai Harn Beach, Phuket' lands on a locality pin 890 m NE; 'หาดในหาน' lands on the beach (4.6, 2,106 reviews), 78 m from the pin. Ao Sane: Phuket101 (Mar 2026) says closed for construction, Thai Holiday Guide (Jul 2026) says open, so it is flagged. Money Shop Nai Harn and Reflections hours from Google.

items.name: Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep
items.tagline: Seafood, island boats and the famous sunset cape
items.description: The working harbour at Phuket's southern tip, not a swimming beach: longtail boats line the shore. People come for the seafood market (buy fish, a restaurant cooks it), boats to Koh Bon, Coral Island and Racha, and a slow local pace with expats, cafes and Muay Thai gyms. Ya Nui and Promthep Cape are a few minutes west.
items.beach: Rawai's own beach is for boats, not swimming. In January go 2 km west to Ya Nui, a small cove with calm water and rocks for easy snorkelling (gear, kayaks and paddleboards for rent).
highlights: Rawai Seafood Market (go around 11:30, before the dinner rush)
Sunset at Promthep Cape
Kayak, paddleboard and snorkel at Ya Nui
Longtail boat to Koh Bon or Coral Island
Chao Ley sea-gypsy village by the pier
items.coordSource: wikidata(Q14217890, 6 m)+google(Ra Wai Beach, 141 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Rawai Beach, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you want a low-cost long-stay base with seafood, gyms and island boats, and will drive to swim.
tips: Older guides list Bermudos (house and techno) in Rawai. We found no 2025-2026 dates: its last listed party was at Shelter, Patong, on 10 May 2024, and its RA page has nothing since 2021. Check its social pages before you plan around it.
Agree the price before you hire a longtail on the beach.
Promthep Cape is very crowded at sunset; the crowd leaves minutes after the sun goes down.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket101 Rawai page (updated 16 Sep 2026) confirms the harbour, the 11:30 market tip, the Chao Ley village, the boats and Ya Nui 2 km west; Ya Nui page: snorkel, kayak and SUP rental. Bermudos: RA promoter 'Bermudos Promo' last event 1 Jan 2021; phangan.events last lists Shelter, 10 May 2024; no RA Thailand listings May 2026-Feb 2027. Pin: Wikidata 6 m, Google 'Ra Wai Beach' 141 m; OSM beach centre is 395 m SW and the seafood market 760 m E.

items.name: Chalong & Soi Ta-iad
items.tagline: Fitness street, big temples and the island-boat pier
items.description: A local area on Chalong Bay, but with no swimming beach. Soi Ta-iad is Phuket's 'fitness street': 1.5 km of Muay Thai and MMA camps (Tiger Muay Thai since 2003), gyms, healthy cafes and long-stay rooms. Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha are close, and many island trips leave from Chalong Pier. You need a scooter or Grab.
items.beach: There is no swimming beach: Chalong Bay is a yacht anchorage and boat pier (in the January wind it is a kitesurf spot), and Kata and Nai Harn are about 15-20 minutes away.
highlights: Train at a Muay Thai camp on Soi Ta-iad
Wat Chalong's 60 m chedi (free, 07:00-17:00)
Big Buddha on Nakkerd Hill (free, 09:00-18:00, reopened 3 March 2026)
Island day trips from Chalong Pier
items.coordSource: osm(Chalong roundabout Clock Tower node 11096744592, 2 m)+google(Chalong roundabout Clock Tower, 7 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Chalong roundabout Clock Tower, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you come to train, want long-stay prices and do not need a beach at your door.
tips: This pin is Chalong Circle. Soi Ta-iad and Wat Chalong are about 3.5 km north of it.
At Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha cover shoulders and knees.
Money Shop and Value Plus both have exchange offices in Chalong.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Big Buddha reopened 3 Mar 2026 after 18 months closed; free, 09:00-18:00, last entry 17:30 (Phuket101, updated 13 Oct 2026; other sites list other hours). Wat Chalong buildings 07:00-17:00, free (Phuket101, Jul 2026). Soi Ta-iad 1.5 km (Phuket101); Tiger Muay Thai founded 2003 (Wikipedia). Kite schools on Chalong Bay (Friendship Beach) work Nov-Mar. Money Shop Chalong Lotus and Value Plus HomePro Chalong open on Google. Pin = Chalong Circle clock tower; OSM 2 m, Google 7 m.

items.name: Phuket Town (Old Town)
items.tagline: Old shophouses, the best food and real local life
items.description: Phuket's capital, a great half-day trip. The Old Town has restored Sino-Portuguese shophouses, Chinese shrines, street art, cafes and some of the best food on the island. Hotels are cheap. Bars are small and relaxed; Courage Bar hosted underground nights in Dec 2025-Feb 2026. The coast is 20-30 minutes away.
items.beach: There is no beach in town. In January drive about 20 minutes to the quiet bays of Cape Panwa (Ao Yon is best for a swim) or 30-40 minutes to Patong, Karon or Kata.
highlights: Sunday Walking Street on Thalang Road (Sun 10 and 17 Jan, from 16:00 to about 21:00-22:00)
Soi Romanee and Thalang Road shophouses
Courage Bar on Bangkok Rd (SUB and FAKE PALM nights in Dec 2025-Feb 2026; check RA for new dates)
Chillva Market (Mon-Sat 17:00-23:00)
Khao Rang Hill viewpoint
items.coordSource: google(Soi Romanee, 26 m)+wikipedia(Phuket Old Town, 165 m)+google(Old Phuket Town, 165 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Phuket Old Town, Phuket
items.stayIf: Stay here if you love food, culture and low prices, and are happy to ride 30 minutes to the beach and the big clubs.
tips: Exchange in town: the SuperRich partner at Suriyadej Circle (Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00) or NC Plus (Mon-Sat 09:00-17:00). Both are closed on Sunday and do not post their rates online.
Mamy Exchange in Koh Kaew, on the airport road, had the best rate we checked (Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00, Sat-Sun 09:00-16:30).
Walk the Old Town early or late; midday is hot and parking is hard. On Sundays Thalang Road and Soi Romanee close to cars from early afternoon.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. RA API lists Courage events on 20 Dec 2025, 2 Jan, 17 Jan, 13 Feb and 19 Feb 2026 (SUB, FAKE PALM) and none after; SUB then used The Chill Spot (Karon, Apr) and Tempo (Chalong, May 2026). Courage is open on Google (Wed-Sun evenings). The Instagram handles in the old text could not be confirmed. Walking Street Sun 16:00-21:00 'and often beyond' (Phuket101, 30 Sep 2026; Google 16:00-22:00). Chillva Mon-Sat 17:00-23:00 (Phuket101 + Google). Exchange hours from Google listings. items.name: Kathu
items.tagline: Local food and jungle fun between Patong and town
items.description: The inland centre of the island, between Patong and Phuket Town. Most visitors drive through, but locals come for the food: Krua Jongjit is in the Michelin Guide, and dim sum breakfasts are cheap. Kathu Shrine is said to be where the Vegetarian Festival began. Golf, a water park, zip-lines and a wake park are here too.
items.beach: There is no beach here; Patong is 10 minutes over the hill, and in January the Kathu waterfall is only a trickle.
highlights: Thai food at Krua Jongjit (Michelin Guide; 11:00 to about 17:30, closed Monday)
Kathu Chinese Shrine
Flying Hanuman zip-line
Andamanda water park
Kathu fresh market

items.name: Cape Panwa
items.tagline: Quiet south-east cape with calm bays and a rooftop sunset
items.description: A green, hilly cape in the south-east, about 20 minutes from Phuket Town. It is quiet: a few resorts, small bays such as Panwa Beach and Ao Yon, small beach restaurants and almost no nightlife. Phuket Aquarium is at the tip. Sri Panwa, the group behind Baba Beach Club, has its resort and the Baba Nest rooftop bar here.
items.beach: In January the sea is calm. Ao Yon is the best public swim (calm all year). The main Panwa Beach (Khao Khad) has dead coral underfoot; the nicer beach further south is for Cape Panwa Hotel guests.
highlights: Sunset at Baba Nest, Sri Panwa (book on Chope)
Phuket Aquarium (08:30-16:30, 300 THB for foreign adults)
Lunch on the sand at Ao Yon Beach
Khao Khad viewpoint tower

items.name: Ao Po & Cape Yamu
items.tagline: Marinas, luxury villas and boats to Koh Yao
items.description: The quiet north-east coast, facing the limestone islands of Phang Nga Bay. Ao Po Grand Marina has yachts, charters and resort boats to Koh Yao Noi (about 40 minutes); public speedboats leave from Bang Rong Pier nearby. Cape Yamu, to the south, has luxury villas and COMO Point Yamu. Almost no shops or nightlife.
items.beach: This is a boat coast, not a beach area; the sea in Phang Nga Bay is calm in January, so come for the views and take a boat to Koh Yao or drive to the west coast to swim.
highlights: Speedboat to Koh Yao Noi from Bang Rong Pier (30-40 min)
Yachts at Ao Po Grand Marina
Sunrise over the islands of Phang Nga Bay
Infinity pool with a bay view at COMO Point Yamu (for hotel guests)

items.name: Thalang
items.tagline: Heritage town, rainforest park and the local DJ scene
items.description: The inland north, the island's historic heart, near the airport. Wat Phra Thong, the Heroines Monument and the Thalang National Museum tell Phuket's history. To the east, Khao Phra Thaeo forest has Bang Pae waterfall, a gibbon project and an elephant sanctuary. Enthusiast Place, a DJ studio, is near Bang Tao.
items.beach: There is no beach here; Bang Tao, Layan and Nai Thon, with calm January seas, are about 15 minutes west.
highlights: Wat Phra Thong, the half-buried Buddha
Thalang National Museum (Wed-Sun 09:00-16:00, 100 THB)
Heroines Monument
Bang Pae waterfall (park fee 200 THB); Gibbon Project visits by booked session only
Enthusiast Place Open Doors (Tuesdays from 19:00, free)

Phuket Elephant Sanctuary is observation only: no riding, bathing or feeding. Book a programme online; the 90-minute Canopy Walkway Tour costs 1,900 THB.
The Gibbon Project opens only for booked learning sessions (10:30, 12:30 or 14:00). On days without bookings it is closed.
The Heroines Monument and the museum are next to each other, about 6 km south of Wat Phra Thong on route 402.

items.name: Natai & Khao Pilai (Phang Nga)
items.tagline: Empty beach, Baba Beach Club and Circoloco Saturdays
items.description: About 10 km of wide, pale sand on the mainland north of the Sarasin Bridge, 35 minutes from the airport. No vendors, sunbeds or jet skis, and only a few resorts, most of them luxury. Baba Beach Club has a Funktion-One sound system and hosts Circoloco on Sat 9 and Sat 16 Jan, 15:00-03:00. You need a car or Grab.
items.beach: From November to April the sea is calm and the shore shelves gently, so January swimming is easy; there is a lifeguard post on the main stretch.
highlights: Circoloco at Baba Beach Club (Sat 9 and Sat 16 Jan, 15:00-03:00)
Baba Beach Club day pass (minimum spend 1,500 THB, 11:00-22:00)
Long, empty beach walks at sunset
Sarasin Bridge viewpoint
Samet Nangshe viewpoint, about 40 minutes away

areas.recommendation: Best base for you: Kamala, at the quiet north end near Café del Mar. You walk to Café del Mar (Pyramid show Fri 8 Jan, Marco Carola Wed 13 Jan, Club Room nights Wed-Sat). By car, Niky's is about 10 minutes, Enthusiast Place about 15, Shelter in Patong about 20, Phuket Old Town about 30, the airport about 35, and Baba Beach Club about an hour. Bang Tao is the same idea with better food and beach clubs, but Shelter is 35 minutes away. Second base: Natai, for the Circoloco Saturdays (9 and 16 Jan, 15:00-03:00). Sleep at or near Baba Beach Club so you walk home at 3 am, and you are 35 minutes from the airport. Pick Patong's north end or Kalim only if you want Shelter or Illuzion on foot several nights; Natai is then about 75 minutes away. Split-stay idea: Fri 8 - Sun 10 Natai (land, Circoloco Sat 9). Sun 10 - Sat 16 Kamala or Bang Tao (Old Town Sunday market Sun 10, Enthusiast open doors Tue 12, Marco Carola Wed 13, Shelter Fri 15). Sat 16 - Mon 18 Natai (Circoloco Sat 16, then 35 minutes to the airport on Monday). Fewer moves: Kamala Fri 8 - Sat 16, then Natai Sat 16 - Mon 18, with a driver booked both ways for Sat 9. January is peak season and hotels cost the most in the first two weeks, so book early.

24 hotels, resumed from the interrupted attempt and filled with targeted checks on 15 Oct 2026. Tiers: 7 luxury, 3 boutique, 8 mid-range, 2 budget, 4 hostel. Areas: Natai 3 (Baba, Aleenta, Natai House) plus the Snug Airportel near the airport as a budget Circoloco base; Kamala, Surin and Bang Tao 5; Patong 3; Kata, Kata Noi and Karon 3; Nai Harn and Rawai 3; Old Town 3; Koh Phangan (Ban Tai) 3.

PRICES: Google Hotels lowest offers for 1 night, checked 15 Oct 2026. Mainly Tue 12 and Sat 16 Jan 2027, plus 9, 10, 14 and 15 Jan from the earlier pass. Hotels use 2 adults; hostels use 1 adult, which gives the bed price. Google returned AED, converted at 15 Oct 2026 rates (1 USD = 33.63 THB = 3.6725 AED). Offers may exclude tax and service charge.
- Circoloco Saturdays (9 and 16 Jan) push Natai prices up 2-3 times. Example: Aleenta is about 19,400 THB on Tue 12 Jan and 45,000-52,000 THB on 9 and 16 Jan.
- Baba Beach Club had no Google rate for any date. Its range comes from a Hotels.com listing for 6-7 Jan 2026 (KRW 576,733-684,581, taxes included).
- See Sea Backpackers price is from undated Hostelworld and Hostelz listings.
- Beyond Kata, Shunli and Natai House showed no rate for some dates. The text says "no online rate", not "sold out".

OPEN CHECK: every listing has Google reviews from 2026 and no closure flag. Coco Garden (Koh Phangan) was dropped because its newest reviews are a year old. ibis Styles Bangtao opened in April 2026 (Accor launch release).

COORDINATES: Google Maps listing pins, cross-checked with OSM (Photon, Overpass or Nominatim), official-site schema data, a Google directions link on the official site (Tented Camp) or Trip.com (Baba). Medium confidence: Natai House and Shunli (Google only) and Lub d (OSM node has no name).

DISTANCES: OSRM foot and car routing (routing.openstreetmap.de). Car times have a traffic buffer added and are rounded.
- OXA distances use the events task's coordinates (9.68693, 100.04643, from OXA's official map link). The previous attempt used an inland pin about 3.8 km away, so these were recomputed.
- Courage Bar's position is a low-confidence street estimate from the events task.

VENUES:
- "Niky's" is Niky's Speakeasy & Nightclub, a techno club on Soi Bang Thao 2 (7.98627, 98.29922). Google 4.5 (56 reviews), latest review about Aug 2026.
- Bermudos' 2026/27 venue is NOT confirmed. Its Google listing in Si Sunthon has only 3-4-year-old reviews and is closed to new posts. Prior research (Tripadvisor, Mixmag) places it in Rawai/Nai Harn (New Reggae Bar). It is mentioned only as a hedged tip on The Nai Harn.

IMAGES: all URLs returned HTTP 200 with an image type. Official photos where the site allowed it. Where official sites block bots or are down, credited Wikimedia Commons area photos are used, marked "(area photo: ...)" in credit: Aleenta, Natai House, Holiday Inn Express, Lub d, Shunli, See Sea. Partner photo URLs from Google listings were not used, because their IDs did not reliably match the property.

REUSED FROM OTHER TASKS: Circoloco dates and times (Dice, Ticketmelon, Baba page), OXA Megatix dates, and Lard Yai walking street hours (Sundays 16:00-22:00).

CONSIDERED, NOT INCLUDED: Sunsuri, Best Western Premier Bangtao, Santhiya Natai, The Talay, Coco Garden.

data.verdict: The best rate we could check is at Mamy Exchange in Koh Kaew, on route 402 between the airport and Phuket Town. On 15 Oct 2026 it paid 33.35 THB per USD 100 note and 37.35 THB per euro, about 0.5% under the mid-market rate. In Patong, use Lion in Jungceylon. In Old Town, use the SuperRich partner at Suriyadej Circle (closed Sundays). Bank booths paid 0.4-1.2% less. ATMs charge 250 THB (Visa) or 350 THB (Mastercard) per withdrawal, so bring clean USD or EUR notes.

atm.feeText: In 2026 Thai bank ATMs charge foreign cards 250 THB per withdrawal with Visa or UnionPay and 350 THB with Mastercard (official fee tables: Kasikorn from 25 Aug 2026, SCB from 1 Sep 2026, Krungsri from 11 Mar 2026). Your home bank may add a fee. One withdrawal is usually 20,000-30,000 THB at most.
cheapest: We found no cheaper bank ATM: Kasikorn, SCB and Krungsri all charge 250 THB (Visa) or 350 THB (Mastercard). A 2026 guide says Bangkok Bank and Krungthai also charge 250 THB.
Use a Visa card if you have one. It saves 100 THB on each withdrawal.
Take out the maximum each time (20,000-30,000 THB). A 250 THB fee is 1.25% of 20,000 THB but 5% of 5,000 THB.
Use ATMs at bank branches or inside malls (Jungceylon, Central Festival). If the machine keeps your card, the bank can help.
tips: If the ATM offers to convert to your home currency, press 'Decline' or 'Without conversion'. Your own bank then converts at a better rate.
Check the fee on the screen before you press OK.
Wise and Revolut cards do not remove the Thai ATM fee of 250/350 THB.
Standalone ATMs in bars and small shops can have lower withdrawal limits.
Withdraw in daylight, cover your PIN, and keep your cash in two places.

cards: Always pay in THB. If a card machine offers your home currency (DCC), say no. On 15 Oct 2026 SCB's card DCC rate was 31.85 THB per USD, while the mid-market rate was 33.50. That is about 5% worse.
Wise and Revolut cards convert close to the mid-market rate. Use them in malls, hotels, for Grab and for bigger bills.
Revolut: do big exchanges on weekdays. Standard plans add about 1% at weekends. Check the free monthly limit of your plan.
You still need cash for taxis, tuk-tuks, markets, beach bars and many small shops. Some places add a fee (often about 3%) for card payments.
Bring two cards from different banks, ideally one Visa and one Mastercard. Keep one card in the hotel safe.
Turn on foreign use in your banking app before you fly.
tips: Best plan: bring clean USD 100 or EUR 100/200 notes and change them at Mamy, Lion or the SuperRich partner. Use ATMs only as a backup.
Big notes get better rates. At Mamy on 15 Oct 2026: USD 50-100 notes 33.35, USD 5-20 notes 33.05 and USD 1-2 notes 32.55 THB.
Notes must be clean: not torn, not written on and not stamped. Old USD 100s get less: on 15 Oct 2026 Ex24 paid 33.08 for old 100s and 33.18 for new ones. Very old or damaged notes can be refused.
Bring your original passport. Changers ask for it and write down the number. Count the baht at the counter and keep the receipt.

Test a rate quickly: for USD 100 notes a good rate is within about 0.5% of the mid-market rate. On 15 Oct 2026 Mamy paid 33.35 when the mid-market rate was 33.50. A booth that pays 33.00 or less is about 1.5% under the mid-market rate.
For USD 1,000 on 15 Oct 2026 you got 33,350 THB at Mamy, 33,220 THB at the ttb bank, 33,070 THB at the SCB bank, and only about 31,850 THB when you paid by card with DCC.

When you arrive, change only a little at the airport or use an ATM there. Mamy is on Thepkrasattri Rd (route 402), on the way from the airport to Phuket Town and Patong. Ask your driver to stop (open Mon-Fri until 17:00, at weekends until 16:30).
In Patong, use Lion in Jungceylon (09:00-21:00). Late at night, the Value Plus booth on Soi Sansabai is open until 04:00.
In Phuket Old Town, use the SuperRich partner at Suriyadej Circle (Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00) or NC Plus (Mon-Sat). Both are closed on Sunday, and 10 Jan and 17 Jan 2027 are Sundays.
In Kata/Karon, Rawai/Nai Harn and Bang Tao/Laguna, use Money Shop, Value Plus or a bank booth. Before you change a big amount, compare with Mamy's live rate on mamyexchange.com.
Natai and Khao Pilai (Phang Nga) have almost no money changers (OpenStreetMap shows none). Bring baht from Phuket.

Green SuperRich Thailand and Vasu Exchange have no Phuket branch: green SuperRich lists only Bangkok and nearby cities, and Vasu has one Bangkok office. The Google pin 'Superrich Money Exchange' on Wirat Hong Yok Rd is not SuperRich: the company there is registered as 'Sunrich Money Exchange'.
On 15 Oct 2026 SuperRich in Bangkok paid 33.43-33.45 for a USD 100 note. Mamy in Phuket paid only about 0.1 THB less.
If you leave the airport in Bangkok (Suvarnabhumi), SuperRich (green and orange) and Value Plus have booths on the B floor by the Airport Rail Link.
Ask for some 100 and 500 baht notes. Taxis and small shops often cannot change 1,000 baht notes.
Changing baht back at a good changer costs little (Mamy sold USD at 33.50 on 15 Oct 2026), but don't change much more than you need.
No Thai bank holiday falls on your dates (8-18 Jan 2027): the only bank holiday in January 2027 is 1 Jan. Some Phuket Town changers close on Sundays (10 and 17 Jan).
avoid: Hotel reception exchange desks: rates are usually much worse.
Airport counters for big amounts: local guides estimate 3-5% worse than town.
Saying yes to your home currency (DCC) at an ATM or card machine: about 5% worse.
Many small ATM withdrawals: you pay 250-350 THB each time.
Bank booths when a top changer is near: on 15 Oct 2026 they paid 0.4-0.8% less for USD and about 1-1.2% less for EUR.
Street booths with a 'No commission' sign but a low rate. Compare the board with the mid-market rate first.
Strangers or Telegram accounts that offer exchange or cash delivery. Mamy says it has no Telegram account, and Money Shop names two fake Telegram accounts.
Changing small, old or damaged notes.
Shops that use the SuperRich name but are not on the official superrich1965.com list.

items.title: TDAC arrival card: required
items.text: Every foreign visitor must fill in the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card online before arrival. You can send it in the 3 days (72 hours) before you land. For 8 Jan, do it on 6 or 7 Jan; the arrival day also works. Have your flight number and hotel address ready. Save the confirmation on your phone.

links.label: Royal Thai Embassy: how to submit the TDAC

items.title: Fake TDAC websites
items.text: Use only tdac.immigration.go.th. Fake sites look official, charge about 20-90 USD and steal passport data. In March 2026 Immigration said about 1 in 10 foreign arrivals had used a fake site. The real TDAC is always free. Immigration's new THIM app is optional. Report fakes to the Cyber Police on 1441.

items.title: Visa-free stay is now 30 days
items.text: Since 15 Sep 2026 the visa-free stay is 30 days (not 60), for tourism only. It covers 60 countries, including all EU states, the UK, US, Israel, Georgia and Ukraine. Russia and Kazakhstan also get 30 days under bilateral deals. Your 8-18 Jan trip fits. Check your passport on the Thai e-Visa site.

items.title: Passport, ticket and money
items.text: Your passport must be valid at least 6 months after arrival and have a free page. Officers may ask for a ticket out of Thailand within 30 days, your hotel booking and proof of money (10,000-20,000 baht per person; sources differ). Checks are random, but some people were refused entry. Keep these papers on your phone.

links.label: Royal Thai Embassy London: visa exemption

items.title: Customs: cigarette limit
items.text: You may bring at most 200 cigarettes (1 carton) per person. Customs checks this on arrival. Above the limit, the cigarettes are usually taken and the fine can be 10 times their value. Vapes and heated-tobacco devices are banned completely (see Safety and law).

items.title: No ETA needed
items.text: The planned Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) has not started (Oct 2026). In 2025 Thailand replaced the plan with the TDAC. If your passport is visa-exempt, the TDAC is the only online form you need before the trip.

items.title: Tourist entry fee: not yet
items.text: A 450-baht entry fee for foreign visitors is planned. The target is early 2027, first for air arrivals. In Oct 2026 it still needed Cabinet approval and a Royal Gazette notice, so it is not in force yet, and the plan can still change. Check the news before you fly.

items.title: Flights via the Middle East
items.text: The UK government warns that the conflict in the Middle East has closed some airspace and caused delays and cancellations (Oct 2026). If your flight goes via the Gulf, check it with your airline before you leave. Make sure your travel insurance covers flight disruption.

items.title: Grab and Bolt
items.text: Both apps work in Phuket and show the price first. Typical car fares: airport to Patong 600-950 baht, Patong to Kata 250-500, Patong to Old Town 400-550. Bolt is often a bit cheaper, so compare. Prices go up at busy times and in heavy rain. If pickup is hard, walk to the main road.

items.title: From the airport
items.text: Grab pickup is near Exit 8 (international) or Exit 1 (domestic). Airport limousine taxis have fixed prices on a board, about 800 baht to Patong; metered taxis add a 100-baht airport fee. Cheapest: Smart Bus (100 baht) to the west-coast beaches, or the Airport Bus (100 baht) to Phuket Town.

items.title: Taxis and tuk-tuks: agree the price first
items.text: Street taxis and tuk-tuks almost never use the meter. They quote fixed prices, often much higher than the apps (Patong to Kata about 500-600 baht; Grab about 250-350). Agree the price before you get in and show the app price to bargain. Carry small notes. If a driver cheats you, call the Tourist Police on 1155.

items.title: Scooter rental: licence and insurance
items.text: To ride legally you need a motorcycle licence from home plus an International Driving Permit that covers motorcycles. Without them, insurance usually pays nothing after a crash. Many rental scooters are not registered, so check the papers. Police checks are common. Never leave your passport as a deposit.

items.title: Helmets and road safety
items.text: Rider and passenger must wear a helmet; since June 2025 the fine is up to 2,000 baht. Thailand drives on the left. Phuket roads are steep, curvy and busy. Do not ride after drinking. After a party, Grab or a taxi is the safer choice.

items.title: Phuket Smart Bus
items.text: Route 1: Airport - Patong - Karon - Kata - Rawai, flat 100 baht. Route 2: Bus Terminal 2 - Phuket Town - Patong, 50 baht. The Dragon Line in Old Town is free. Pay by contactless card, Thai QR or cash. Last bus from the airport 23:30; last bus from Rawai to the airport 19:30.

links.label: Smart Bus timetable and live tracking

items.title: Local songthaew buses
items.text: Open-sided songthaew buses leave Ranong Road (near the market) in Phuket Town for the main beaches, about every 30 minutes from about 06:00 to 18:00. They cost about 30-50 baht but are slow and do not run in the evening.

items.title: Typical drive times
items.text: From the airport: Patong 50-90 min, Kata 60-90 min, Old Town 40-60 min, Natai (Phang Nga) 30-45 min. Patong to Kata 20-30 min, Patong to Old Town 30-45 min. Traffic is worst in the late afternoon, so leave early for flights.

items.title: Koh Phangan: fastest (fly + boat)
items.text: There is no direct boat. Fly Phuket - Koh Samui with Bangkok Airways (55 min, 6-7 flights a day, about 3,000-5,000 baht one way in late 2026). From Samui airport, a Lomprayah van + boat goes to Koh Phangan: about 500 baht, or 700 to your hotel, 1-2 hours. Door to door about 5 hours.

items.title: Koh Phangan: one bus + boat ticket
items.text: Lomprayah sells one ticket: bus to Donsak pier, then a fast boat. Pickup about 07:30 at hotels in Patong, Kata, Karon, Rawai and Nai Harn, or 10:00 at Phuket airport. You reach Koh Phangan about 16:30. About 1,600 baht, or 1,800 with hotel drop-off (2026 timetable). Book a few days ahead.

items.title: Koh Phangan: cheapest and slowest
items.text: Public bus from Phuket Bus Terminal 2 to Surat Thani (about 4 hours), van to Donsak pier (about 1 hour), then a ferry to Thong Sala (about 2.5 hours). Total about 8-9 hours and roughly 600-900 baht. Only worth it on a tight budget.

items.title: Party trips: book early
items.text: Flights, boats and rooms on Koh Phangan sell out around big party dates. Book early and check the last boat back. Koh Phangan's rainy season is usually November to March, so rain and rough seas are more likely there than in Phuket. Do not plan a tight connection to a flight home.

items.title: Phi Phi ferries from Rassada Pier
items.text: Big ferries leave Rassada Pier (near Phuket Town) at about 08:30, 11:00, 13:30 and 15:00. They take about 2 hours and cost about 500-700 baht. Speedboats take about 1 hour for 750-850 baht. Pay the 20-baht island fee in cash at Tonsai pier.

items.title: Maya Bay and park fee
items.text: Trips to Maya Bay and Phi Phi Le pay a national park fee: 400 baht for foreign adults, 200 for children. Some tours include it, others collect cash on the day. Swimming at Maya Bay is not allowed. The bay closes every year from 1 Aug to 30 Sep, so it is open in January.

items.title: Krabi and Ao Nang
items.text: Boats also run from Rassada Pier to Ao Nang in Krabi. The fastest speedboats take about 1-1.5 hours; ferries that stop at Phi Phi take much longer. Schedules change by season, so check times on 12Go.

items.title: Day tours: Chalong and Ao Po piers
items.text: Many speedboat day tours (Phi Phi, Racha, Coral Island) leave from Chalong Pier in the south. Some boats leave from Ao Po Grand Marina in the north-east. Most tours include hotel pickup. Ask which pier before you book.

items.title: How to book boats
items.text: Book on 12Go or on the official sites (Lomprayah, Seatran, Bangkok Airways). Save e-tickets offline. Arrive at the pier 30-45 minutes early to swap the e-ticket for a boarding pass.

items.title: Tourist SIM or eSIM
items.text: AIS and True sell tourist plans with unlimited 5G/4G data. AIS 2026 prices: 8 days 499 baht, 15 days 699 baht. True: 15 days 699, 30 days 1,199. For 8-18 Jan (11 days) the 15-day plan fits. You need your passport to register.

items.title: Airport counter or eSIM before you fly
items.text: AIS and True counters are in the international arrivals hall at Phuket airport. Or buy an AIS or True eSIM online before the trip, or use an eSIM app such as Airalo. Check that your phone supports eSIM. Keep your home SIM on for bank SMS codes.

items.title: Wi-Fi
items.text: Most hotels, cafes and malls have free Wi-Fi. AIS tourist plans include AIS Super WiFi hotspots. Signal can be weak on boats and small islands, so download maps and tickets before you go.

items.title: Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal
items.text: It is illegal to bring, own or use any vape, e-cigarette, pod, e-liquid or heated-tobacco device (like IQOS). There are no exceptions for tourists. Penalties: confiscation, fines of about 5,000-30,000 baht, detention and court. You may have to stay in Thailand until the case ends. Leave it at home.

items.title: Drugs: very strict laws
items.text: Even small amounts of drugs can mean heavy fines, prison, deportation and a ban from Thailand. Police raid parties and villas, also on Koh Phangan, and do urine tests; a positive test can lead to charges. Serious cases can mean life in prison or the death penalty. Never carry anything for others.

items.title: New deportation rules
items.text: Since 28 Aug 2026 Thailand can deport foreigners without a criminal conviction if officials decide their behaviour is against public order or public morals. People who are deported may not be allowed back. Follow local laws and police instructions.

links.label: UK travel advice: safety and law

items.title: Cannabis: medical use only
items.text: Since June 2025 cannabis is for medical use only: you need a Thai prescription (max 30-day supply). Recreational use is illegal, even though you still see shops. Do not smoke in public. Taking cannabis out of Thailand is a crime: fines from 30,000 baht per kg and an immigration watchlist.

items.title: Drink spiking and fake alcohol
items.text: At parties, never leave your drink alone and do not accept open drinks from strangers. Methanol in fake or cheap spirits can kill; get help fast if someone has blurred vision or feels very sick after drinking. Plan your ride home before you go out.

items.title: Alcohol sale hours
items.text: Shops and most bars may sell alcohol from 11:00 to midnight; the old 14:00-17:00 ban has ended. Licensed hotels, clubs and airports may serve outside these hours. The legal drinking age is 20. Since Nov 2025, drinkers can also be fined up to 10,000 baht for drinking at banned times or places.

items.title: No smoking on the beach
items.text: Since 2018 smoking is banned on Patong Beach and other listed Thai beaches: fine up to 100,000 baht and/or up to 1 year in jail. Use the marked smoking areas and never leave cigarette butts. Smoking in other public places can also bring a fine of up to 5,000 baht.

links.label: The Nation: Patong beach smoking ban

items.title: Jet-ski scams
items.text: Some jet-ski operators blame tourists for old damage and ask for big money. Never leave your passport as a deposit. Film the jet ski from all sides before you ride. If there is a dispute, stay calm and call the Tourist Police on 1155.

items.title: Rip currents and flags
items.text: In January the west-coast sea is usually calm, but rip currents still happen. Swim near lifeguards and never swim at a red flag. If a current pulls you out, do not fight it: swim parallel to the beach, then back in. Do not swim drunk or at night.

items.title: Drones need permits
items.text: Register every drone with the NBTC within 30 days of arrival; camera drones also need CAAT registration (with a Thai SIM). You need 1 million baht third-party insurance and CAAT approval at least 3 days before each flight. No flying within 9 km of airports. Unregistered drone: up to 100,000 baht and/or 5 years in jail.

items.title: Carry ID
items.text: Police can ask to see your passport. Carry it, or at least a copy of the photo page and entry stamp. A copy is usually fine, but you may have to show the original at a police station within 24 hours.

items.title: Bangkok Hospital Phuket (private)
items.text: Large private hospital in Phuket Town (2/1 Hongyok Utis Road) with English-speaking staff and a 24-hour emergency room. Emergency: 1719 from a Thai number, or +66 76 254 425. It is expensive, so have travel insurance.

items.title: Bangkok Hospital Siriroj (private)
items.text: Big private hospital of the same group, on the bypass road near Central Phuket (44 Chalermprakiat Ror 9 Road). English-speaking staff and a 24-hour emergency room. Phone +66 76 361 888; emergency 1719 from a Thai number.

items.title: Mission Hospital Phuket (private)
items.text: Mid-size private hospital at 4/1 Thepkrasattri Road in Phuket Town, with a 24-hour emergency room. Usually cheaper than the Bangkok Hospital group. Phone +66 76 237 220.

items.title: Vachira Phuket Hospital (government)
items.text: Phuket's main government hospital (353 Yaowarat Road, Phuket Town) with a 24-hour emergency and trauma centre. Cheaper, but waits can be long and English can be limited. Phone +66 76 361 234.

items.title: Patong Hospital (government)
items.text: Small government hospital in Patong (57 Sai Nam Yen Road), the closest hospital to Bangla Road. It has a 24-hour emergency room for first care; serious cases go to the big hospitals in Phuket Town. Phone +66 76 342 633.

items.title: Ambulance and insurance
items.text: Call 1669 for an ambulance (191 also works). Hospitals ask for a payment guarantee or insurance before treatment. Get travel insurance that covers hospital, evacuation and your activities (boats, diving, scooter only with a valid licence). Save the insurer's phone number.

items.title: Pharmacies
items.text: Pharmacies are everywhere, including Boots and Watsons in malls. Many basic medicines are sold without a prescription. Do not buy medicine on the street; it may be fake. Bring your own medicines in the original packs with a copy of the prescription.

items.title: Sun and heat
items.text: In January the midday UV index is high to extreme (about 8-11). Use high-SPF sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses, and stay in the shade around midday. Drink plenty of water, especially at parties. Heat stroke can be deadly.

items.title: Mosquitoes and dengue
items.text: Dengue fever exists in Thailand. The mosquitoes bite mostly in the daytime. Use repellent with 20% or more DEET and sleep in air-con or screened rooms. See a doctor if you get a high fever. Ask your doctor about vaccines such as hepatitis A before the trip.

items.title: Tap water and animals
items.text: Do not drink tap water; drink bottled or filtered water. Keep away from stray dogs and monkeys, as rabies exists. If an animal bites or scratches you, wash the wound with soap and water and see a doctor the same day.

items.title: Dry, hot and sunny
items.text: January is one of the driest months in Phuket. The average high is about 32-33°C and the low about 23-25°C. Rain is about 30-36 mm in the whole month, on about 5-6 days, and a short shower is always possible. Humidity is about 70-76%.

items.title: Sea conditions
items.text: On the west coast (Patong, Karon, Kata, Bang Tao) the Andaman Sea is usually calm and clear in January. The water is about 28°C. It is the best season for swimming, snorkelling and boat trips, but still check the beach flags.

items.title: Sunrise and sunset
items.text: During your trip, sunrise is 06:42-06:45 and sunset 18:23-18:28 (on 12 Jan: 06:43 and 18:25). It gets dark about 20-25 minutes after sunset. West-coast beaches face the sunset.

items.title: Peak season
items.text: January is high season. Prices are highest over Christmas and New Year and stay high all month. Popular tours, boats and good rooms fill up fast, so book the important things early.

items.title: Temples: dress code
items.text: Cover shoulders and knees: no tank tops, short shorts or short skirts. Take off your shoes before you enter a temple building. Do not point your feet at a Buddha image. Some temples lend sarongs at the entrance.

items.title: Royal family: show respect
items.text: Never criticise or joke about the King or the royal family, also not online. It is a crime with long prison terms. Stand when the royal anthem plays, for example in cinemas before the film. Do not step on money, because it shows the King.

items.title: Shoes, head and feet
items.text: Take off your shoes when you enter homes, temples, massage rooms and some shops; if you see shoes at the door, do the same. Do not touch people's heads. Do not point your feet at people or put them on tables.

items.title: The wai
items.text: The wai is the Thai greeting: palms together at the chest and a small bow. Return a wai from adults. You do not need to wai staff or children; a smile and sawasdee krap or ka is fine. Women should not touch monks.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Tipping is not required but welcome. Many hotels and restaurants add a 10% service charge, so check the bill. Round up taxi fares. Leave about 50-100 baht for a massage or a good guide.

items.title: Haggling
items.text: Bargain at markets, with tuk-tuks and for tours sold on the street. Do not bargain in malls, 7-Eleven, restaurants or shops with fixed prices. Smile and stay calm; anger and shouting do not work in Thailand.

items.title: Plugs and voltage
items.text: Thailand uses 220-230 V, 50 Hz. Most sockets take flat US-style pins (type A/B) and round two-pin European plugs (type C). UK and Australian plugs need an adapter. Phone and laptop chargers marked 100-240 V work fine.

items.title: Grab, Bolt and inDrive
items.text: Install Grab and Bolt before you arrive and add a payment card. Compare both for each ride. inDrive also works in Phuket and lets you offer your own price.

items.title: Google Translate with offline Thai
items.text: Download Thai for offline use in Google Translate. The camera mode reads menus and signs, and conversation mode helps with drivers.

items.title: Google Maps offline area
items.text: Download offline maps of Phuket and Phang Nga (and Koh Phangan if you go). Save your hotel and favourite places. Show the map to drivers to explain where you want to go.

items.title: LINE
items.text: LINE is the main chat app in Thailand. Many hotels, drivers, tour shops and clubs answer on LINE faster than by email or phone.

items.title: 12Go
items.text: Book ferries, buses, vans and domestic flights, with e-tickets on your phone. Check the pier and pickup time carefully.

items.title: Klook and GetYourGuide
items.text: Book tours, boat trips and tickets with reviews and clear prices. Check what is included (hotel pickup, park fees, lunch) and the cancellation rules.

items.title: Wise and ATMs
items.text: A Wise or similar card gives a good exchange rate. In 2026 Thai bank ATMs charge foreign cards 250 baht (Visa) or 350 baht (Mastercard) per withdrawal, so take out larger amounts. Always choose to pay in baht (THB), not in your home currency.

items.title: Thailand Tourist Police app
items.text: Official app with an SOS function that connects you to the Tourist Police (1155) and uses GPS to find you. It works without a Thai SIM. Live chat in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Russian.

emergencyNumbers.note: Scams, theft, disputes. Also via the SOS function in the Thailand Tourist Police app.

emergencyNumbers.note: Can also send an ambulance or fire service.

emergencyNumbers.note: From Thai numbers. From any phone: +66 76 254 425.
